nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of natural numbers, this is the number $\max S + 1$, where the maximum of the empty set is taken to be $0$. It is strictly greater than every element of $S$.
nodes.title: Strict upper bound of a finite set of naturals

nodes.summary: The bound-variable supremum of a type scheme $\sigma$ is one more than the largest index $i$ of a bound variable occurring in $\sigma$, and $0$ if no bound variable occurs in $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Bound-variable supremum of a type scheme

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a name, and let $\sigma'$ and $\sigma$ be type schemes such that $\sigma'$ is more general than $\sigma$. Then the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma'$ in front of $\Gamma'$ is more general than the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma$ in front of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Extending more general contexts by a binding

nodes.summary: A typing context over base types $B$ is a finite list of bindings $(x, \sigma)$, each pairing a name $x$ (a string) with a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$. A name may be bound more than once; the first binding of a name in the list is the visible one.
nodes.title: Typing context

nodes.summary: Given maps $f$ and $g$ from natural numbers to monotypes over $B$, a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$ evaluates to the monotype obtained by replacing each free type variable $x$ of $\sigma$ by $f(x)$ and each bound variable $i$ by $g(i)$, keeping every base type $b$ unchanged. An arrow $\sigma_1 \to \sigma_2$ evaluates to the arrow from the evaluation of $\sigma_1$ to the evaluation of $\sigma_2$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a type scheme

nodes.summary: An expression is a variable $x$, an application $e_1\,e_2$, an abstraction $\lambda x.\, e$, or a let-binding $\mathsf{let}\ x = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$, where $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$ are expressions and variable names $x$ are strings.
nodes.title: Expressions of the λ-calculus with let

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ give every name $x$ the same visible scheme (or both bind no scheme to $x$), then $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables.
nodes.title: Free type variables depend only on visible bindings

nodes.summary: The free type variables of a typing context $\Gamma$ are the type variables occurring free in the visible scheme of some name bound in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Free type variables of a context

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables, then for every monotype $\tau$ the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ equals the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma'$.
nodes.title: Generalization depends only on the free variables of the context

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that every free type variable of $\Gamma'$ is a free type variable of $\Gamma$, and let $\tau$ be a monotype. Then the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma'$ is more general than the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Generalizing in a context with fewer free variables

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $\tau$ a monotype and $s$ a type substitution. Write $s\Gamma$ for the context obtained by applying $s$ to every scheme of $\Gamma$, and let $N$ be one more than the largest free type variable of $s\Gamma$, with $N = 1$ if $s\Gamma$ has none. Let $\rho$ be the substitution sending a type variable $y$ to $s(y)$ if $y$ is free in $\Gamma$, and to the type variable $y + N$ otherwise.…
nodes.title: Renaming step of the substitution lemma

nodes.summary: Given a typing context $\Gamma$ and a monotype $\tau$, the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$ is the type scheme obtained from $\tau$ by turning each type variable $\alpha$ that is not free in $\Gamma$ into the bound variable with index $\alpha$, while type variables free in $\Gamma$ stay free.
nodes.title: Generalization of a monotype

nodes.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, all variable names $f$ and $x$, and every type variable $\alpha$, the expression $\mathtt{let}\ f = \lambda x.\, x\ \mathtt{in}\ f\, f$ has type $\alpha \to \alpha$ in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: `let` generalizes

nodes.summary: For every expression $e$ and monotype $\tau$, if type inference for closed expressions returns $\tau$ on $e$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the empty context.
nodes.title: Soundness of type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $n$ a natural number. If Algorithm W, run on $\Gamma$ and $e$ with fresh-variable counter $n$, succeeds and returns a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the context $s\Gamma$ obtained by applying $s$ to every type scheme of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Soundness of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $x$ a name and $\tau$ a monotype. Then $\Gamma \vdash x : \tau$ holds for the variable expression $x$ if and only if there are a type scheme $\sigma$ and monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that the lookup of $x$ in $\Gamma$ gives $\sigma$ and $\tau$ is the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$.
nodes.title: Typing inversion for variables

nodes.summary: The syntax-directed Damas–Milner typing relation $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ between a context $\Gamma$, an expression $e$ and a monotype $\tau$ is the least relation closed under the following rules, where $\Gamma, x : \sigma$ is $\Gamma$ extended by the binding $x : \sigma$ in front.
nodes.title: Hindley–Milner typing

nodes.summary: If an expression $e$ has a monotype $\tau'$ in the empty context, then type inference succeeds on $e$ and returns a monotype $\tau$ of which $\tau'$ is a substitution instance: $\tau' = r(\tau)$ for some type substitution $r$.
nodes.title: Completeness of type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: Type inference succeeds on an expression $e$ if and only if $e$ has some monotype in the empty context.
nodes.title: Type inference succeeds exactly on typable closed expressions

nodes.summary: The inferred type of a closed expression is one of its types, and every type of it is an instance of the inferred one.
nodes.title: Principal types

nodes.summary: Type inference on an expression $e$ runs Algorithm W on $e$ in the empty context with fresh-variable counter $0$. If W succeeds with a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, the inferred type of $e$ is $\tau$; if W fails, $e$ has no inferred type.
nodes.title: Type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: For every type substitution $s$, every scheme $\sigma$ and all monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, instantiating each bound variable $i$ of $s(\sigma)$ by $s(t_i)$ gives $s$ applied to the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$. Here $s$ acts on a scheme through its free type variables only.
nodes.title: Instantiation commutes with substitution

nodes.summary: Given monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, the instance of a scheme $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$ is the monotype obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing each bound variable $i$ by $t_i$, keeping its free type variables and base types unchanged.
nodes.title: Instantiation of a type scheme

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $s$ a type substitution, $x$ a variable name, $e_1, e_2$ expressions and $\tau_1, \tau_2$ monotypes, and write $s\Gamma$ for the context obtained by applying $s$ to every type scheme of $\Gamma$. Suppose $e_1$ has type $\tau_1$ in $\Gamma$, and $e_2$ has type $\tau_2$ in the context obtained from $s\Gamma$ by binding $x$, in front, to the type scheme that results from applying $s$…
nodes.title: The let rule under a type substitution

nodes.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ agree on every free type variable of a context $\Gamma$, then for every name $x$ the lookups of $x$ in $s(\Gamma)$ and in $t(\Gamma)$ are equal: both give no scheme, or both give the same scheme.
nodes.title: Substitutions agreeing on a context give the same lookups

nodes.summary: The lookup of a name $x$ in a typing context $\Gamma$ is the scheme of the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$ (the visible one), or nothing if $\Gamma$ has no binding of $x$.
nodes.title: Context lookup

nodes.summary: If $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ and $\Gamma'$ is a context more general than $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma' \vdash e : \tau$.
nodes.title: Typing is preserved in more general contexts

nodes.summary: A context $\Gamma'$ is more general than a context $\Gamma$ when the same names are visible in both and, for each such name $x$, the visible scheme of $x$ in $\Gamma'$ is more general than its visible scheme in $\Gamma$. Only lookups matter, so shadowed bindings play no role.
nodes.title: More general context

nodes.summary: A scheme $\sigma'$ is more general than a scheme $\sigma$ when every instance of $\sigma$ is also an instance of $\sigma'$ and every free type variable of $\sigma'$ is a free type variable of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: More general type scheme

nodes.summary: For all monotypes $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, $\tau_1 \ne (\tau_1 \to \tau_2)$.
nodes.title: No monotype is an arrow out of itself

nodes.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, every variable name $f$ and every monotype $\tau$, the judgment $\Gamma \vdash \lambda f.\, f\, f : \tau$ does not hold.
nodes.title: The abstraction $\lambda f.\, f\, f$ has no type

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ give the same lookup result for every name $x$ (the same visible scheme, or none in both), then $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Contexts with the same lookups are related by generality

nodes.summary: A type scheme over base types $B$ is a term over the constant set $B \oplus \mathbb{N}$: its variables $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$ are the free type variables, a constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$ is the base type $b \in B$, a constant $\mathrm{inr}\, i$ is the bound variable $i$, and a node of two schemes is an arrow.
nodes.title: Type schemes

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $\tau$ a monotype with $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$. Then for every type substitution $s$, $s\Gamma \vdash e : s\tau$, where $s\Gamma$ applies $s$ to every scheme of $\Gamma$ and $s\tau$ applies $s$ to $\tau$.
nodes.title: Hindley–Milner typing is stable under type substitution

nodes.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ satisfy $s(x) = t(x)$ for every free type variable $x$ of a type scheme $\sigma$, then applying $s$ to $\sigma$ gives the same scheme as applying $t$.
nodes.title: Substitution into a scheme depends only on its free variables

nodes.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$, a monotype $\tau$ and a type substitution $r$, the scheme obtained by applying $r$ to the free type variables of the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ is more general than the generalization of $r(\tau)$ in $r(\Gamma)$: every instance of the latter is an instance of the former, and every free type variable of the former is a free type variable of the latter.
nodes.title: Substituting into a generalization is more general

nodes.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a type scheme $\sigma$, $s\sigma$ is the scheme obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing every free type variable $x$ with the monotype $s(x)$, read as a scheme with no bound variables. The bound variables of $\sigma$ are left unchanged.
nodes.title: Applying a type substitution to a scheme

nodes.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a typing context $\Gamma$, $s\Gamma$ is the context obtained by applying $s$ to the scheme of every binding of $\Gamma$, keeping the names and their order.
nodes.title: Applying a type substitution to a context

nodes.summary: Every monotype $\tau$ is read as the type scheme with no bound variables of the same shape: a type variable stays the same type variable, a base type $b$ becomes the constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$, and an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ becomes the arrow of the images of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$.
nodes.title: Monotypes as type schemes

nodes.summary: A monotype over a set $B$ of base types is a term over the constants $B$: a type variable $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$, a base type $b \in B$, or an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ of two monotypes (a binary node).
nodes.title: Monotypes

nodes.summary: A term $t$ has all its variables below $n$ when every variable $z$ occurring in $t$ satisfies $z < n$.
nodes.title: Variables below a bound

nodes.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$ and a name $x$, this is the set of free type variables of the scheme that $\Gamma$ binds to $x$ (the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$), or the empty set if $\Gamma$ does not bind $x$.
nodes.title: Free type variables of a name's visible scheme

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context and $n$ a natural number such that every free type variable of $\Gamma$ is less than $n$. If, for some type substitution $u$, an expression $e$ has a monotype $\tau'$ in the context $u(\Gamma)$, then Algorithm W succeeds on $\Gamma$ and $e$ with counter $n$, returning a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a new counter $n'$, and there is a type substitution $r$ such that…
nodes.title: Completeness of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context and $n$ a natural number such that every free type variable of $\Gamma$ is less than $n$. If Algorithm W succeeds on $\Gamma$ and an expression $e$ with counter $n$, returning a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a new counter $n'$, then $n \le n'$, every type variable of $\tau$ is less than $n'$, and for every type variable $x < n$ every type variable of $s(x)$ is less than…
nodes.title: Freshness invariants of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: Given a typing context $\Gamma$, an expression $e$ and a counter $n$, Algorithm W either fails or returns a substitution, a monotype and a new counter; type variables $\alpha_m$ with $m \ge n$ serve as fresh. Write $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ for the arrow type, $s\Gamma$ for $\Gamma$ with the substitution $s$ applied to every type scheme, and $s(\tau)$ for $s$ applied to a monotype $\tau$. Algorithm W is defined by…
nodes.title: Algorithm W
Logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
